whatItDoes: Converts JPG, PNG, WebP, GIF, BMP images into a multi-page PDF — one image per page — with reorderable pages, page-size (A4/Letter/Fit), orientation, and margin controls. All rendering is client-side via pdf-lib and canvas.
whyItExists: Creating a PDF from images typically means uploading photos to a server. This tool embeds images locally, scales them to fit the page while preserving aspect ratio, and lets you control page geometry without any upload.
whoShouldUse: Students turning phone photos into a PDF assignment, professionals creating portfolios, and anyone needing a quick image-to-PDF without cloud risk.
useCases: Convert 10 phone photos into an A4 portrait PDF for submission
Reorder 5 screenshots by dragging before converting to PDF
Use Fit size to create a PDF where each page matches the image dimensions
Choose Letter landscape with medium margin for a slide-like PDF
instructions: Drop or select up to 30 images (JPG/PNG/WebP/GIF/BMP, 10MB each). Each shows dimensions.
Drag cards or use up/down to set page order — page number badge updates.
Pick Page size (A4, Letter, Fit), Orientation (ignored for Fit), and Margin (None/Small/Medium).
Click Convert to PDF — images are embedded centered and scaled to fit the printable area.
Download the PDF from the green card showing page count and size.
examples: Input: 3 images (1200×800, 800×600, 1920×1080) → A4 portrait, small margin → Output: 3-page PDF with each image centered and fitted.
Input: 1 2000×1500 PNG → Fit size, no margin → Output: single-page PDF exactly 2000×1500 pt plus zero margin.
bestPractices: Use A4/Letter for printing, Fit for screen viewing where page size should match image
Set margin to None only for full-bleed images; Small is safer for printers
WebP/GIF are converted via canvas to PNG before embedding — verify transparency if needed
commonMistakes: Expecting metadata/EXIF to transfer — the PDF embeds pixel data only
Uploading 30 × 10MB images may hit 50MB total limit and trigger an error
Assuming Fit preserves file size — Fit creates one page per image; large images still embed at full resolution
faq: Are images uploaded? No — conversion uses pdf-lib and canvas in your browser. Images never leave your device.
How are images sized? Each image is scaled uniformly to fit the page's printable area (page minus margins) and centered.
Does it support WebP? Yes — WebP/GIF/BMP are rasterized via canvas then embedded as PNG.
Can I mix orientations? Each page can have a different image aspect; page orientation is global (A4/Letter) or per-image if Fit is chosen.
features: Images to PDF, one per page, with drag reorder
A4 / Letter / Fit page sizes with margin control
Supports JPG, PNG, WebP, GIF, BMP
